# Pandora Papers: Mapping King Abdullah II’s Reported Offshore Property Network

## Executive summary

The Pandora Papers reporting describes a property-holding network associated with Jordan’s King Abdullah II. The network allegedly used offshore companies—primarily incorporated in the British Virgin Islands (BVI)—to acquire and hold luxury real estate in the United States and United Kingdom. The reported properties include three Malibu, California, residences; three Washington, D.C., condominiums; and several properties in and around London, including Belgravia, together with a house in Ascot. The overall value was reported as exceeding $100 million, although the sources use different counts and valuation methods. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))

The reported corporate structure connects King Abdullah II to at least 16 companies identified in an internal 2017 memorandum from the Panamanian law firm Alcogal. DW separately reported that the properties were acquired through 36 front companies registered in tax havens. This difference may reflect different counting methods, different points in time, or different categories of entities; the supplied sources do not resolve the discrepancy. ([S1](https://www.dw.com/en/pandora-papers-the-king-of-jordans-hidden-property-gems/a-59403014); [S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))

The strongest documented ownership link is the Guardian’s account of an Alcogal compliance memorandum identifying a Jordanian client named “Abdullah Al Hussein,” born on January 30, 1962, with an address at Raghadan Palace—the birth date and address associated in the reporting with King Abdullah II. The memorandum reportedly identified him as the beneficial owner of 16 companies holding assets in the United States, United Kingdom, and Jersey. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))

The reporting does not establish that the properties were purchased with public funds, foreign aid, or proceeds of crime. The king’s lawyers and the Royal Hashemite Court denied misuse of public money and said the assets were purchased from personal wealth. The offshore ownership and property purchases are therefore best characterized as documented investigative allegations concerning secrecy, beneficial ownership, and political accountability—not as proven criminal conduct. ([S1](https://www.dw.com/en/pandora-papers-the-king-of-jordans-hidden-property-gems/a-59403014); [S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal); [S3](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/3/investigation-reveals-offshore-assets-of-heads-of-state))

## Scope and source assessment

This report uses four source identifiers:

| Source ID | Publication | Main evidentiary contribution |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Deutsche Welle, October 4, 2021 | Summary of the offshore-property allegations, reported number of entities, political context, and official responses |
| S2 | The Guardian, October 3, 2021 | Detailed account of the ownership memorandum, named companies, locations, purchase prices, and Alcogal compliance records |
| S3 | Al Jazeera, October 3–4, 2021 | Independent summary of the Pandora Papers investigation and the Royal Court and lawyers’ responses |
| S4 | URL supplied as an ICIJ link | The supplied text duplicates the Al Jazeera article rather than presenting a distinct ICIJ article; it is not treated as independent corroboration |

The Guardian provides the most detailed account of the network because it identifies the alleged beneficial-owner record, the service provider, three company names, and several property transactions. DW and Al Jazeera broadly corroborate the existence of the reported network and the official denials. The evidence is nevertheless based on journalistic reporting about leaked records rather than publicly reproduced corporate filings in the material supplied here.

## Network overview

### Principal alleged beneficial owner

The reported central individual is King Abdullah II of Jordan. The Guardian stated that an Alcogal internal memorandum from February 2017 identified a Jordanian national named “Abdullah Al Hussein,” born January 30, 1962, and associated with “Raghadan Palace,” as the beneficial owner of 16 companies. The Guardian linked those identifying details to King Abdullah II. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))

DW reported that the monarch was referred to in trust-firm communications as the “final beneficiary” and, in one exchange, as “you know who” from Jordan. This language suggests that the advisers were discussing the ultimate beneficiary indirectly, but it does not by itself prove why the euphemistic wording was used. ([S1](https://www.dw.com/en/pandora-papers-the-king-of-jordans-hidden-property-gems/a-59403014))

### Offshore service provider and advisers

The principal offshore adviser identified in the reporting is Alcogal, a Panamanian law firm. According to the Guardian, its compliance managers circulated an internal memorandum concerning the Jordanian client and the 16 companies. The Guardian also reported that Alcogal staff discussed how to protect the king’s confidentiality and apparently did not identify him in internal documents as a politically exposed person (PEP), although the firm disputed any deliberate failure to classify him properly. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))

A separate adviser was DLA Piper, the law firm representing the king in responses to the reporting. DLA Piper rejected any implication that offshore ownership was improper and stated that King Abdullah had not misused public money or aid proceeds. DLA Piper’s role in the evidence supplied is that of legal representative and spokesperson, not an entity shown to have incorporated or administered the companies. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal); [S3](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/3/investigation-reveals-offshore-assets-of-heads-of-state))

### Jurisdictions

The network’s reported jurisdictions include:

- **British Virgin Islands:** The Guardian reported that the companies were incorporated in the BVI. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))
- **Panama:** Alcogal, the reported service provider, is described as a Panamanian law firm. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))
- **Jersey:** The Guardian stated that the 16 companies held assets in the United States, United Kingdom, and Jersey. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))
- **United States and United Kingdom:** These were the principal real-estate jurisdictions, with assets in California, Washington, D.C., London, and Ascot. ([S1](https://www.dw.com/en/pandora-papers-the-king-of-jordans-hidden-property-gems/a-59403014); [S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))

The sources refer to these jurisdictions as offshore or tax-haven locations, but the presence of a company in an offshore jurisdiction does not itself establish tax evasion, money laundering, or another offense. Both the Guardian and Al Jazeera expressly noted that offshore ownership can be lawful. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal); [S3](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/3/investigation-reveals-offshore-assets-of-heads-of-state))

## Reported shell companies and property links

The Guardian specifically named three entities: Nabisco Holdings SA, Setara Limited, and Timara Limited. According to the reporting, these companies acquired the three Malibu properties. The sources supplied do not provide incorporation dates, directors, shareholding percentages, or complete corporate chains for these entities. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))

| Reported entity | Reported function or asset link | Jurisdictional connection | Evidence status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nabisco Holdings SA | One of the companies associated with the Malibu properties | Offshore corporate structure; the broader companies were reported as BVI entities | Reported by the Guardian; complete filing details not supplied |
| Setara Limited | One of the companies associated with the Malibu properties | Offshore corporate structure | Reported by the Guardian; complete filing details not supplied |
| Timara Limited | One of the companies associated with the Malibu properties | Offshore corporate structure | Reported by the Guardian; complete filing details not supplied |
| Other unnamed entities | Reported to hold Washington, D.C., and UK property assets | United States, United Kingdom, Jersey, and offshore jurisdictions | Reported generally; individual company-to-property links not supplied |

The Guardian reported that the three Malibu properties were acquired through three offshore companies, including Nabisco Holdings SA, Setara Limited, and Timara Limited. It stated that the principal Malibu property was purchased in August 2014 for $33.5 million and that the two neighboring properties were subsequently acquired. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))

## Real-estate locations and reported values

### Malibu, California

The most prominent reported acquisition was a large clifftop property on Malibu’s coast. The Guardian described it as a 26-room, “resort hotel-like mega mansion.” Public records reportedly showed that the property had previously passed from Hollywood producers to dot-com billionaires before its reported acquisition by King Abdullah II in August 2014 for $33.5 million. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))

Al Jazeera reported that three Malibu beachfront mansions were purchased through three offshore companies for a combined $68 million. The Guardian’s account gives the $33.5 million price for the principal mansion but does not, in the supplied text, provide the individual prices of the two neighboring properties. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal); [S3](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/3/investigation-reveals-offshore-assets-of-heads-of-state))

### Washington, D.C.

The Guardian reported that King Abdullah acquired three condominiums in Washington, D.C., between 2012 and 2014 for a combined $13.8 million. Al Jazeera described the units as luxury apartments with panoramic views of the Potomac River. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal); [S3](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/3/investigation-reveals-offshore-assets-of-heads-of-state))

### London and Ascot

The Guardian reported that the network included seven luxury UK properties purchased between 2003 and 2011. Three were in Belgravia, London, and the portfolio had an estimated current market value of approximately £28 million. Al Jazeera additionally referred to a house in Ascot and multimillion-dollar apartments in central London. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal); [S3](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/3/investigation-reveals-offshore-assets-of-heads-of-state))

### Aggregate count and valuation

DW reported that the monarch purchased 14 houses and apartments in the United States and United Kingdom between 2003 and 2017 for more than €91 million, or approximately $106 million at the exchange rate used in the article. The Guardian described the portfolio as worth “well in excess of $100m.” These figures are broadly consistent in scale but are not identical because one appears to refer to acquisition prices while the other emphasizes estimated current value and an overall portfolio assessment. ([S1](https://www.dw.com/en/pandora-papers-the-king-of-jordans-hidden-property-gems/a-59403014); [S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))

## Official explanations and unresolved issues

The Royal Hashemite Court said that the properties were owned by the king personally and were used for diplomatic visits, consultations, and some private visits. It attributed nondisclosure to security and privacy concerns. The court also said that the properties and related expenses were not funded by the state treasury, foreign grants, or loans received as foreign assistance. ([S1](https://www.dw.com/en/pandora-papers-the-king-of-jordans-hidden-property-gems/a-59403014); [S3](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/3/investigation-reveals-offshore-assets-of-heads-of-state))

The king’s lawyers said the source of the wealth was personal and denied the misuse of public funds or aid. They also argued that high-profile individuals commonly use offshore companies for privacy and security. The reporting does not provide an independent financial audit tracing the source of the purchase funds. Consequently, the claim that the assets were privately funded remains an official assertion within the evidence supplied, not a conclusively demonstrated fact. ([S1](https://www.dw.com/en/pandora-papers-the-king-of-jordans-hidden-property-gems/a-59403014); [S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))

The Guardian reported that the king’s lawyers said he was not required to pay taxes under Jordanian law. The supplied material does not establish whether taxes were owed or paid in the United States, United Kingdom, BVI, Jersey, or other relevant jurisdictions. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))

## Contradictions and evidentiary limitations

Several differences appear in the reporting:

1. **Number of companies:** DW reported 36 front companies, while the Guardian identified 16 companies in the 2017 Alcogal memorandum. The sources do not explain whether the 36 figure includes companies outside the 16, inactive entities, or entities counted under a different methodology. ([S1](https://www.dw.com/en/pandora-papers-the-king-of-jordans-hidden-property-gems/a-59403014); [S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))

2. **Number of properties:** DW reported 14 houses and flats, while the Guardian’s detailed account explicitly identifies three Malibu properties, three Washington condominiums, and seven UK properties—13 properties in the categories described. The Guardian also refers to an Ascot house, which may account for the difference, but the supplied text does not clearly reconcile the totals. ([S1](https://www.dw.com/en/pandora-papers-the-king-of-jordans-hidden-property-gems/a-59403014); [S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))

3. **Value:** Al Jazeera reported $68 million for the three Malibu properties, whereas the Guardian specified $33.5 million for the principal property and did not list the two neighboring purchase prices. The figures are not necessarily inconsistent, because one is a combined figure and the other is for one property. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal); [S3](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/3/investigation-reveals-offshore-assets-of-heads-of-state))

4. **ICIJ source-link problem:** The supplied ICIJ URL contains text identical to the supplied Al Jazeera article rather than a distinct ICIJ page. It therefore cannot be used as independent corroboration in this report. ([S3](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/3/investigation-reveals-offshore-assets-of-heads-of-state); [S4](https://www.icij.org/investigations/pandora-papers/jordan-king-abdullah-luxury-property/))

## Assessment

The evidence supports a concrete conclusion: public reporting mapped a sophisticated offshore ownership structure connecting King Abdullah II, Alcogal, BVI-linked companies, and luxury real estate in Malibu, Washington, D.C., London, and Ascot. The most significant evidence is not merely that the king owned expensive properties, but that the properties were reportedly held through corporate vehicles designed to keep the beneficial owner from public view. The Alcogal memorandum and the matching name, birth date, and Raghadan Palace address provide the strongest reported link between the companies and the monarch. ([S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))

My assessment is that the reporting establishes a credible and extensively documented case of concealed beneficial ownership and offshore asset structuring, but it does **not** establish, on the supplied evidence, that King Abdullah II committed tax evasion, money laundering, corruption, or misuse of foreign aid. The central public-interest issue is therefore transparency and the political contrast between a large privately held international property portfolio and Jordan’s reliance on foreign assistance and austerity, rather than a proven criminal offense. ([S1](https://www.dw.com/en/pandora-papers-the-king-of-jordans-hidden-property-gems/a-59403014); [S2](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal))

## References

Deutsche Welle. (2021, October 4). *Pandora Papers: The royal “you know who” from Jordan*. [DW website](https://www.dw.com/en/pandora-papers-the-king-of-jordans-hidden-property-gems/a-59403014)

The Guardian. (2021, October 3). Goodley, S., & Safi, M. *King of Jordan hidden property empire worth more than $100m, Pandora papers reveal*. [The Guardian website](https://www.theguardian.com/news/2021/oct/03/king-of-jordan-hidden-property-empire-worth-more-than-100m-pandora-papers-reveal)

Al Jazeera. (2021, October 3–4). *Jordan king exposed over tax havens and luxury homes*. [Al Jazeera website](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/10/3/investigation-reveals-offshore-assets-of-heads-of-state)

International Consortium of Investigative Journalists. (URL supplied; retrieved text duplicates the Al Jazeera article). *Jordan king exposed over tax havens and luxury homes*. [ICIJ URL](https://www.icij.org/investigations/pandora-papers/jordan-king-abdullah-luxury-property/)
